notes: Strongest result: SEAT's own MY12 'IBIZA' owner's manual (6J4012003DC, edition 12.11, reprint 15.12.11) at seat.co.uk/datamanual-manual/ibiza/my12_w45/en-uk/Ibiza_EN.pdf - a 'general manual for the IBIZA' (SC and ST have separate documents) - states verbatim that QG1 = LongLife and QG0/QG2 = time/distance-dependent, and that the fixed regime is '1 year / 15 000 km (whatever comes first)'; identical wording in the MY11 and MY13 editions (MY13 adds '(10 000 miles)'). The owner's manuals do not print per-item intervals (oil, brake fluid, pollen filter all defer to the 'Maintenance Programme' booklet, which was not found online; Haynes covers only 1.2 engines for this generation). No official SEAT document with a timing-belt interval for CGGA/CGGB was found; forum/Autodata-derived figures cluster at 5 years / 60,000 miles (older 1999-2010 Autodata text and a BXW thread), or 'check at 90,000 km then every 30,000 km' (BXW owner's manual quote). Third-party engine-specific rows (cararac 'Ibiza 1.4 16V (63 kW)' 6J: oil 15000 km/12 months, brake fluid 24 months; iDGARAGES '1.4i 85 16V 2008-05 à 2012-01': service 12 months/15,000 km, cabin filter 24 months/30,000 km, brake fluid first at 36 then every 24 months) are consistent with the official fixed regime. Engine codes CGGA/CGGB are not printed in the official PDFs (SEAT manuals list engines by kW only). The PDFs were downloaded by the fetch tool and text was extracted to stdout; page numbers given as both printed manual page and PDF page.
